news.headline: Why Oracle Stock Is Up Today
news.summary: Oracle shares jumped roughly 9% intraday on Nov 11 to around $128 as AI cloud stocks rebounded, bouncing off the two-year low of about $109 set on Nov 6. Benzinga also pointed to a record peak-demand reduction by Oracle's Opower utility software, though the move looked mostly like a sector-wide relief rally.

news.headline: Oracle breaks ground on roughly $2B Nashville world headquarters campus
news.summary: Oracle scheduled the groundbreaking of its River North world headquarters in Nashville for November 10, an estimated $2B campus with about 2 million sq ft of office space that it calls a hub for AI innovation. The start goes ahead despite this year's large layoffs, which had raised doubts about the plan.

news.headline: Bernstein Reiterates Outperform on Oracle's AI Growth
news.summary: Bernstein's Mark Moerdler kept Oracle as a top pick with an Outperform rating and $325 target after updating his 10-year model, arguing both the AI data-center unit and the core database business are AI winners. He said Oracle should not need further funding and is about 18 months from positive free cash flow, naming OpenAI's IPO and the FCF turn as catalysts.

news.headline: Microsoft reportedly winding down 2023 deal to rent AI cloud capacity from Oracle
news.summary: Bloomberg reported that Microsoft is winding down a 2023 arrangement to rent AI computing capacity from Oracle's cloud as it shifts to its own data center buildout. Coming two days after the Tencent cancellation, it was the second lost non-OpenAI customer in a week and the stock fell about 4%.

news.headline: Oracle abandons $7 billion Tencent AI chip-leasing deal under US government pressure
news.summary: Per the FT, Oracle walked away from the roughly $7B agreement, reported in early October, to lease about 100,000 advanced AI chips to Tencent from offshore data centers, after pressure from the Trump administration. The cancellation removes a sizable non-OpenAI customer from the backlog and the shares fell on the news.

news.headline: Oracle Announces Pricing of $20 Billion of Common Stock and Senior Notes
news.summary: Oracle sold 86.2M shares at $116 (about $9.9B net) plus $10B of senior notes in five tranches with coupons of 7.00% (2029) to 8.65% (2046), closing November 4. The raise uses the entire $20B FY27-FY30 new-funding cap set just five days earlier at Investor Day, and the stock dropped on the dilution and high borrowing cost.

news.headline: Oracle Investor Day 2026: $225B FY30 revenue target, $20B funding cap and path to positive free cash flow
news.summary: Oracle reaffirmed FY27 guidance (revenue of at least $90B, non-GAAP EPS of $8.10) and set FY30 targets of $225B+ revenue, 40%+ non-GAAP operating margin and $21+ EPS, with free cash flow turning positive in H2 FY28 and at least $30B in FY29. It capped new capital-market funding through FY30 at $20B (ex-refinancing), and the stock jumped about 11%.

catalysts.label: Annual Meeting of Stockholders
catalysts.detail: Virtual annual meeting at 9:00 a.m. CT on November 18, 2026 (announced November 6); replay on the IR site through November 25.

catalysts.label: Fiscal Q2 2027 earnings
catalysts.detail: Projected date (calendar estimates range from about Dec 10 to Dec 14 after the close); not yet confirmed by Oracle, which usually sets the date in late Nov/early Dec. Company guide: revenue $21.00-21.64B, non-GAAP EPS $1.83-1.91. First print after Investor Day and the $20B raise; focus on RPO/backlog after the Tencent cancellation, OCI growth, capex and cash burn against the reaffirmed FY27 guide of $90B+ revenue and $8.10 non-GAAP EPS.

catalysts.label: Project Jupiter power resolution
catalysts.detail: Whether the force-majeure situation at the $165B New Mexico campus is resolved and power/permitting issues are cleared; delays here push out OpenAI-linked capacity and revenue recognition.

catalysts.label: Fiscal Q3 2027 earnings
catalysts.detail: Expected mid-March 2027 based on Oracle's usual calendar; next checkpoint on capacity ramp and progress toward the FY27 targets.

catalysts.label: Free cash flow turns positive (company target)
catalysts.detail: Investor Day target: FCF positive in the second half of FY28 and at least $30B in FY29, with net debt below 3.5x adjusted EBITDA in FY29 and growth self-funded from then on. Any slippage would likely force funding beyond the $20B cap, which is already fully used.

pulse: Oracle rebounded about 9% intraday on Nov 11 to roughly $128 in a broad AI cloud relief rally, after sliding to a two-year low near $109 on Nov 6 and briefly trading below the $116 price of its $20B equity-and-debt raise; Benzinga notes the chart is still close to a death cross. Sell-side support is holding (Bernstein Outperform/$325, UBS Buy/$250, Stephens Overweight/$213), while bears focus on the dropped $7B Tencent deal, Microsoft winding down its AI capacity rental, OpenAI concentration in the ~$664B backlog and high leverage. Next up are the Nov 18 annual meeting and the fiscal Q2 report expected around December 10-14 (not yet confirmed), where RPO, OCI growth and capex versus the FY27 guide will be in focus.
